The **governor of Tokyo** ([Japanese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_language "Japanese language"): 東京都知事[Hepburn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hepburn_romanization "Hepburn romanization"): _Tōkyō-To Chiji_) is the head of government of [Tokyo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokyo "Tokyo").
In 1943, upon the unification of [Tokyo City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokyo_City "Tokyo City") and [Tokyo Prefecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokyo_Prefecture_\(1868%E2%80%931943\) "Tokyo Prefecture \(1868–1943\)") into [Tokyo Metropolitan Government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokyo_Metropolitan_Government "Tokyo Metropolitan Government"), the position of Governor was created. Previously, the prefecture had a Governor while the City had [a Mayor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayors_of_Tokyo "Mayors of Tokyo"). The current title was adopted in 1947 due to the enactment of the Local Autonomy Law.
## Overview
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Governor_of_Tokyo&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Overview")]
The Governor of Tokyo is the head of the [Tokyo Metropolitan Government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokyo_Metropolitan_Government "Tokyo Metropolitan Government"), and is elected by the citizens of [Tokyo Metropolis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokyo "Tokyo") every four years, most recently in the [2024 Tokyo gubernatorial election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Tokyo_gubernatorial_election "2024 Tokyo gubernatorial election").
As [Tokyo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokyo "Tokyo") has the largest economy and population in the country, government policies can greatly affect national affairs, giving a governor significant influence in the country and a louder voice in the National Governors' Association.
The annual budget of [Tokyo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokyo "Tokyo") is about 13 trillion yen, ten times that of other prefectures and comparable to the national budget of [Indonesia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indonesia "Indonesia"), so a governor also has a great deal of influence in the [national economy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economy_of_Japan "Economy of Japan").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_of_Tokyo#cite_note-1) The [Tokyo Metropolitan Government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokyo_Metropolitan_Government "Tokyo Metropolitan Government") has more than 160,000 employees, making it by far Japan's largest employer.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_of_Tokyo#cite_note-auto-2)
## Qualifications
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Governor_of_Tokyo&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Qualifications")]
Candidates must be a citizen of [Japan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japan "Japan") and be a resident of [Tokyo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokyo "Tokyo") for more than three months, and must be over the age of 30. Candidates must also put up three million yen to the [Tokyo Metropolitan Government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokyo_Metropolitan_Government "Tokyo Metropolitan Government"), which will only be returned if they receive at least 10% of the votes.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_of_Tokyo#cite_note-3)
